Room to compose

The old board was too short for several tops and skirts, even at their movement limits. This candidate keeps the same paper width on a phone and adds vertical room.

3.6 × 2.7 → 3.6 × 4.2. Four pieces remain the limit. The PNG now follows the portrait board at 1800 × 2100.

What stays intact

Published v1 saves load without moving the pieces or rewriting storage. Captured geometry, paper offsets, accessories, layer order, removal/Undo, reload, storage failure protection and composite export passed regression checks. Existing paper artwork is unchanged: all 46 front/back raster hashes matched the published source.

Tests cover desktop, 390 × 844 and 320 × 568 portrait, plus landscape touch emulation. They do not establish physical-phone/Safari feel. The taller board gives a smaller overview on a short landscape screen; portrait is the preferred composition view.

Owner phone check

  1. Make a top and bottom, move them apart, then bring the waist join closer.
  2. Try full tilt, dragging and cancelling a touch.
  3. Scroll the tools, remove/Undo, reload and save the portrait PNG.

This comparison file is self-contained and does not read or change saved boards. Interactive candidate testing should use a separate local or approved private-preview origin before any production merge.

Next designs

Defer new geometry commissions until this composition space feels right on the owner's phone. Copyable separate Claude/Grok briefs are prepared for one garment, one accessory and one or two coordinating papers each, with material visibility maps, offset compatibility, front/back renders and clear curated/experimental labels. Two or three outfits and mannequin forms need a separate design decision.
